title: Mastering OCT: The Retina & Optic Nerve Blueprint
summary: A high-fidelity guide to Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) interpretation, integrating cross-sectional retinal anatomy, quantitative RNFL metrics, and the latest biomarkers for macular and glaucomatous disease. Designed for the advanced clinician to navigate the nuances between 'Red Disease' and true pathology.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Physics
sections.content: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a non-invasive, non-contact imaging modality employing low-coherence interferometry (usually near-infrared light ~840nm) to produce high-resolution cross-sectional 'optical biopsies'. Time-Domain (TD) is obsolete; Spectral-Domain (SD) uses a spectrometer to achieve 5µm resolution, while Swept-Source (SS-OCT) uses a tunable laser at ~1050nm for deeper penetration into the choroid.

rows: Thickest at poles; thins in glaucoma
Disrupted in AMD, CNV, or CSR

sections.title: Systematic Macular Interpretation
content: Step 1: Check Signal Strength (Must be >6/10 for reliability).
Step 2: Evaluate Foveal Contour (Normal dip vs. flattening vs. elevation).
Step 3: Analyze Intra-retinal Space (Check for cysts, exudates, hemorrhage).
Step 4: Inspect the EZ & RPE line (Look for 'shagginess' or pigment epithelial detachments).
Step 5: Review Quantitative Maps (Compare Central Subfield Thickness to normative data).

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Worry
content: Sub-retinal Fluid (SRF): Indicator of active CNV, CSR, or VKH.
Intra-retinal Cysts (IRC): Hallmarks of DME, RVO, or post-cataract Irvine-Gass.
Hyper-reflective Foci: Migratory RPE cells or hard exudates; indicates chronicity and inflammation.
Full Thickness Macular Hole (FTMH): Immediate surgical referral if symptomatic.
Nasal Stepping on RNFL: High specificity for early glaucomatous damage.
Bilateral Diffuse Thinning: Consider neuro-ophthalmic causes (e.g., toxic, nutritional, or compressive optic neuropathy).

sections.title: The Pitfalls: Why Your Scan is 'Red'
content: Segmentation Error: Software misidentifies layers due to high myopia or dense media.
Decentration: The scan is not centered on the fovea/disc, mimicking focal loss.
Media Opacities: Cataracts or vitreous hemorrhage reduce signal, causing false thinning.
Axial Length: High myopes often show 'Red Disease' due to temporal shift of the bundles.
Vitreous Floaters: Casting shadows (signal drop-off) interpreted as RNFL loss.

content.explanation: Normal Neuroretinal Rim thickness order: Inferior (thickest) > Superior > Nasal > Temporal (thinnest). Reversal often indicates glaucoma.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workflow: Glaucoma
content: 1. Clinical Correlate: Look at the Disc first.
2. Check RNFL Thickness: Look for focal 'V-shaped' defects.
3. Ganglion Cell Analysis: Check the Macula (parafoveal thinning).
4. Functional Correlation: Match OCT defects to Humphrey Visual Field (HVF).
5. Progression Analysis: Guided Progression Analysis (GPA) over 3+ scans.

rows: Splitting of layers, often in RNFL/OPL

sections.title: Ancillary Testing Integration
content: OCT-Angiography (OCT-A): Visualize flow without dye; detects CNV membranes.
Fundus Fluorescein Angiography (FFA): Gold standard for 'leakage' vs 'pooling'.
Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF): Detects metabolic stress (RPE health) in GA or dystrophies.
Enhanced Depth Imaging (EDI): Specifically used to measure choroidal thickness.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Residents
content: The 'Bruch's Membrane Opening' (BMO) is the true anatomic edge of the optic nerve.
A 'Floor Effect' occurs when RNFL reaches ~50µm; OCT cannot measure further loss accurately.
Temporal thinning is common in non-glaucomatous optic atrophy (e.g., Toxic/Nutritional).
Always look at the 'En Face' image to ensure the scan line crossed the lesion of interest.

sections.title: Recent Advances: AI & Deep Learning
sections.content: Artificial Intelligence algorithms (like Google Health and various FDA-approved platforms) are now capable of autonomous screening for Diabetic Retinopathy and predicting CNV conversion in AMD. Future OCT systems will likely integrate 'Fluid Volume' quantification as a routine metric for treatment intervals (Treat-and-Extend).

sections.title: Landmark Studies: The OCT Impact
content: OHTS: Demonstrated that thinner corneas (CCT) are risk factors, but OCT provides the structural proof of damage.
CATT/HARBOR: Established OCT as the primary tool for monitoring anti-VEGF response.
ALTS: Highlights the importance of structural vs. functional discordance in early glaucoma.
